title: HPV16 E7 Interactome Proteomics After Anisomelic Acid Treatment
projectDescription: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a major cause of cervical and other anogenital cancers, with the viral oncoprotein E6 playing a central role in carcinogenesis. We previously demonstrated that anisomelic acid treatment reduces E7 protein levels in HPV-positive cancer cells. Here, we employed mass spectrometry-based proteomics to characterize changes in the HPV16 E7 interactome in normal oral keratinocytes following anisomelic acid treatment.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Co-immunoprecipitated samples were processed using an on-bead digestion protocol. Beads were digested with 5 µg/mL trypsin in six volumes of 2 M urea, 25 mM ammonium bicarbonate (ABC, pH 7.5) at 27 °C with shaking at 800 rpm for 30 minutes. The supernatant was collected, and beads were washed twice with 2.5 volumes of 2 M urea, 25 mM ABC, and 1 mM DTT. All supernatants were pooled and digested overnight at room temperature. Following digestion, peptides were alkylated for 30 minutes in the dark with iodoacetamide (IAA), acidified with trifluoroacetic acid, and desalted using a Sep-Pak C18 96-well plate (40 mg, Waters). Desalted peptides were dried and reconstituted in 0.1% formic acid, and 400 ng of each sample was subjected to LC–MS/MS analysis. LC–MS/MS was performed on an EASY-nLC 1200 HPLC system (Thermo Fisher Scientific) coupled to an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific) equipped with a nano-electrospray ionization source. Samples were loaded onto a trap column (100 µm i.d. × 2 cm) and separated on an analytical column (75 µm i.d. × 15 cm), both packed in-house with ReproSil-Pur C18-AQ resin (3 µm, 120 Å, Dr. Maisch GmbH). Peptides were eluted over a 60-minute gradient at 300 nL/min as follows: 8–21% solvent B over 28 min, 21–36% B over 22 min, 36–100% B over 5 min, followed by a 5-minute wash at 100% B. Solvent B consisted of 80% acetonitrile and 0.1% formic acid in water. Full-scan MS spectra were acquired in the Orbitrap at a resolution of 120,000 (m/z 300–1750), with an AGC target of 700,000 and a maximum injection time of 50 ms. Precursor ions with charge states > +2 and intensities > 25,000 were selected for fragmentation within a 2.5-second cycle. Fragmentation was performed by higher-energy collisional dissociation (HCD) with a normalized collision energy of 27%. MS/MS spectra were acquired in the Orbitrap at a resolution of 30,000, with an AGC target of 50,000 and a maximum injection time of 75 ms. Dynamic exclusion was set to 35 seconds with a mass tolerance of 10 ppm.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw LC–MS/MS data were analyzed using either MaxQuant (version 2.0.1.0) or FragPipe (version 21.1) with MSFragger (version 4.0), IonQuant (version 1.10.12), and Philosopher (version 5.1.0). For MaxQuant processing, spectra were searched against a UniProt database containing Human papillomavirus proteins (UP000009251; 9 entries) and the human proteome (UP000005640; 78,120 entries), downloaded on August 1, 2021. Methionine oxidation and N-terminal acetylation were set as variable modifications, and cysteine carbamidomethylation as a fixed modification. Trypsin/P was specified as the digestion enzyme, allowing up to two missed cleavages. The precursor mass tolerance was 20 ppm for the first search and 4.5 ppm for the main search. Label-free quantification (LFQ) was enabled with a minimum ratio count of 2, using unique and razor peptides for quantification. A false discovery rate (FDR) of 1% was applied at both peptide and protein levels. The match between runs feature was enabled with a 2-minute matching time window and a 20-minute alignment window. For FragPipe processing, spectra were searched against the UniProt human proteome (UP000005640; downloaded September 5, 2023; 40,912 entries, including 50% reverse decoys). The default LFQ-MBR workflow was applied with precursor and fragment mass tolerances of 20 ppm. Trypsin digestion allowing up to two missed cleavages was used. Methionine oxidation was specified as a variable modification, and cysteine carbamidomethylation as a fixed modification. Peptide and protein FDR thresholds were set to 1%.
